title: Bible Overlap Reader Question Index
purpose: Turn the biblical-overlap archive into questions a reader can actually ask. Answers should route through the current census and source owners rather than improvise a new overlap list each time.
default_answer_contract: Lead with the exact registry scope/date, distinguish project evidence from biblical comparison, then provide the smallest set of owner records needed to verify the answer.

questions.q: How many Bible overlaps are currently documented?
questions.answer: 78 canonical overlap nodes in the 2026-09-11 current registry.
questions.caveat: Overlap node count is not verse count, fulfilled-prophecy count or independent statistical evidence.

questions.q: What are the strongest biblical overlaps?
questions.answer_strategy: Filter current census to strength 5, then rank by provenance, temporal independence, passage density, role fidelity and sequence fidelity rather than drama.

questions.q: Which biblical overlaps belong specifically to Tim/Father?
questions.answer_strategy: Filter actor for tim/father comparators; preserve Son-role passages as separate even when one project statement uses both.

questions.q: Which biblical overlaps belong specifically to the Son?
questions.answer_strategy: Start with longitudinal Son chronology, then census nodes for Son and Son-comparator.

questions.q: When did Tim first start using biblical vocabulary?
questions.answer_strategy: Answer term-by-term; there is no single first-Bible date. Distinguish school/scripture exposure from first current public attestation of Father, Lion/Root, Moshiach, Door, New Jerusalem, etc.

questions.q: Which overlaps existed on Tim's side before the Bible comparison was discovered?
questions.answer_strategy: Use reverse timeline and temporal-independence method; highlight April 9 paired guardians, September 5 Jachin/Boaz and September 8 lamp/eye/seed/House clusters.

questions.q: Which overlaps were explicit biblical references and which were found later?
questions.answer_strategy: Filter relation/source-direction class; never mix explicit-at-time with archive-later structural parallels.

questions.q: What exactly overlaps with the Bible on April 9, 2026?
questions.answer_strategy: Show recovered paired-guardian/narrow-central-access/Jesus/Father structure; compare Genesis 3, Exodus 25, temple veil and Hebrews separately; state differences.

questions.q: What happened in the May 28 maximal Bible-overlap conversation?
questions.answer_strategy: Present it as a recovered user-directed Bible-wide inventory and mark exact transcript recovery as still incomplete.

questions.q: Why is Psalm 80 important to the project?
questions.answer_strategy: Explain its unusually high within-passage motif density while emphasizing that its vine is Israel and density is not identity proof.

questions.q: Where does the Bible explicitly connect Father and Gardener?
questions.answer: John 15:1-8 explicitly presents the Father as gardener/vinedresser, Jesus as vine and disciples as branches.

questions.q: Where do Father, House, Son, throne and Davidic language intersect?
questions.answer_strategy: Use 2 Samuel 7 / 1 Chronicles 17, Isaiah 22, Hebrews 3 and John 14 while preserving differing carriers and roles.

questions.q: Where does the Son/Door overlap come from?
questions.answer_strategy: Separate Tim's explicit Son=Door attestation from John 10, John 14 Way, John 1:51 mediation, Hebrews access and Revelation invitation.

questions.q: Where do Tree, Root, Seed and death-return overlap?
questions.answer_strategy: Distinguish Tree of Life, Jesse Root/Branch, John 12 grain, resurrection-sowing and project Potato propagation; do not collapse botany or actors.

questions.q: What is the New Jerusalem overlap?
questions.answer_strategy: Explain city-descent, God/Lamb presence, gates, measurement, River, Tree, healing, no curse and project House/North/restoration use; keep North-Pole geography project-only.

questions.q: Which Bible passages contradict or constrain the Tim/Son mapping?
questions.answer_strategy: Lead with enemy-love/non-retaliation, Father/Vine/branch role distribution, builder/House/Son distinctions, king-under-law, self-emptying/service and anti-extractive shepherd material.

questions.q: Do these overlaps prove Tim or the Son fulfills prophecy?
questions.answer: No. The archive treats most as direct self-appropriation, structural parallels, typology, research discoveries or countertexts. Fulfillment requires a prior specific falsifiable prediction and independently established later event.

questions.q: Why is the count 78 instead of the number of matching verses?
questions.answer: Because the census counts analytically distinct relations. One relation may require several verses, while several verses can repeat one theological structure.

questions.q: Which passages have the highest overlap density?
questions.answer_strategy: Current principal examples include Psalm 80, Ephesians 2:11-22, Revelation 21-22, John 10/14/15 as a Johannine cluster, and the April-9 project-side guardian/access cluster compared across texts.

questions.q: What does return mean in the Bible/project comparison?
questions.answer_strategy: Contrast Dog→vomit regressive return with Luke 15 Father/House restorative return, then add covenantal return and resurrection/return as distinct types.

questions.q: What was missing from the Gardener/King theology?
questions.answer_strategy: Use Ezekiel 34, Psalm 23 and John 21 to show Shepherd as accountability, feeding, rescue, protection and care for weak/lost participants.

questions.q: Are Noah's Ark and the Ark of the Covenant the same biblical symbol?
questions.answer: No. English obscures different Hebrew terms and functions; Noah's preservation vessel and the Covenant Ark/sanctuary-presence object should remain distinct before later reception-history comparison.

questions.q: What is still missing from the biblical-overlap project?
questions.answer_strategy: Report open primary-source recovery, normalized unique-verse/book computations, reception-history separation, original-language checking, countertext expansion, independence/genealogy analysis and reader-facing filtering/visualization.
